get_user.title: Get the signed-in user
get_user.description: Read the user the connection's token belongs to -- their username, every attribute on the account, and their MFA settings. The cheapest call that proves the token is still valid.

output.description: The user's username, attributes and MFA configuration.

update_user_attributes.title: Update the signed-in user's attributes
update_user_attributes.description: Change attributes on the user's own account. `user_attributes` is a list of {"Name": ..., "Value": ...} pairs -- standard names are prefixed like "email", "phone_number", "given_name", and custom ones like "custom:tenant_id". Changing `email` or `phone_number` usually puts it back into an unverified state and sends a code, which verify_user_attribute then confirms.

user_attributes.description: The attributes to set, each {"Name": "email", "Value": "ada@example.com"}. Only the attributes you send are changed.

client_metadata.description: Extra key/value data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers, not stored on the user.

output.description: Which attributes now need verification, with the delivery medium used for each code.

delete_user_attributes.title: Delete attributes from the signed-in user
delete_user_attributes.description: Remove attributes from the user's own account by name. Required attributes cannot be deleted, and clearing a verified email or phone number affects how the user can sign in and recover the account.

user_attribute_names.description: Names of the attributes to remove, e.g. ["custom:nickname"].

output.description: Empty on success -- Cognito answers 200 with no fields.

change_password.title: Change the signed-in user's password
change_password.description: Change the user's own password, proving knowledge of the current one. Rejected if `proposed_password` fails the pool's password policy, and the user's other sessions are not signed out by this alone.

proposed_password.description: The new password. Must satisfy the user pool's password policy.

delete_own_account.title: Delete the signed-in user's account
delete_own_account.description: Permanently delete the user's own account from the pool. Irreversible, and it takes their attributes, devices and MFA registrations with it -- the user cannot sign in again afterwards.

global_sign_out.title: Sign the user out everywhere
global_sign_out.description: Invalidate every refresh token the user holds, across all devices. This connection's own tokens are included, so it will need to re-authorize afterwards.

get_user_auth_factors.title: List the user's available sign-in factors
get_user_auth_factors.description: Read which authentication factors are usable for this user -- password, email or SMS one-time code, passkey -- which is what a client needs to offer the right sign-in options.

output.description: The user's username and their available authentication factors.

send_attribute_verification_code.title: Send a verification code for an attribute
send_attribute_verification_code.description: Have Cognito send a verification code to the user's email or phone so that attribute can be marked verified. This sends a real message to a real person.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

output.description: Where the code was sent -- the medium and the masked destination.

verify_user_attribute.title: Verify an attribute with its code
verify_user_attribute.description: Confirm an email address or phone number using the code Cognito sent. Until this succeeds the attribute stays unverified, which can block password recovery.

code.description: The verification code the user received.

set_mfa_preference.title: Set the user's MFA preferences
set_mfa_preference.description: Choose which second factors are enabled for the user and which is preferred -- SMS, TOTP, email or passkey. Each setting is {"Enabled": true, "PreferredMfa": true}; enabling TOTP requires the authenticator to have been registered first with associate_software_token and verify_software_token.

sms_mfa_settings.description: SMS second factor, e.g. {"Enabled": true, "PreferredMfa": false}.

software_token_mfa_settings.description: TOTP second factor, e.g. {"Enabled": true, "PreferredMfa": true}.

email_mfa_settings.description: Email one-time-code second factor, in the same shape.

webauthn_mfa_settings.description: Passkey (WebAuthn) second factor, in the same shape.

associate_software_token.title: Start registering an authenticator app
associate_software_token.description: Begin TOTP enrolment. The response's `SecretCode` is what the user's authenticator app scans or types; the enrolment is not complete until verify_software_token succeeds with a code from that app.

session.description: A challenge session from an in-flight sign-in, when enrolling during authentication rather than for an already signed-in user.

output.description: The TOTP secret to give the authenticator app, and the session to continue with.

verify_software_token.title: Finish registering an authenticator app
verify_software_token.description: Complete TOTP enrolment by proving the app is generating the right codes. Only after this can TOTP be made the preferred factor.

user_code.description: The current code from the user's authenticator app.

session.description: The session returned by associate_software_token, if you used one.

friendly_device_name.description: A name for the authenticator, shown to the user later.

output.description: Whether the token was accepted, and the session to continue with.

list_devices.title: List the user's remembered devices
list_devices.description: Read the devices Cognito has remembered for this user. A remembered device can skip MFA, so this list is worth auditing.

limit.description: How many devices to return, up to 60.

pagination_token.description: Token from a previous response, to fetch the next page.

output.description: The remembered devices and the token for the next page.

get_device.title: Get a remembered device
get_device.description: Read one remembered device -- its key, name and last authenticated time.

update_device_status.title: Remember or stop remembering a device
update_device_status.description: Change whether Cognito treats a device as remembered, which decides whether MFA is skipped on it. Setting it to not_remembered tightens security on that device immediately.

device_remembered_status.description: Whether the device should be remembered.

forget_device.title: Forget a device
forget_device.description: Remove a device from the user's remembered list. The next sign-in from it is treated as new, so MFA applies again.

list_webauthn_credentials.title: List the user's passkeys
list_webauthn_credentials.description: Read the WebAuthn credentials (passkeys) registered for this user, with their names and creation dates.

output.description: The registered passkeys and the token for the next page.

start_webauthn_registration.title: Start registering a passkey
start_webauthn_registration.description: Begin passkey enrolment. The response holds the WebAuthn creation options the browser passes to `navigator.credentials.create()`; the result comes back through complete_webauthn_registration.

complete_webauthn_registration.title: Finish registering a passkey
complete_webauthn_registration.description: Complete passkey enrolment with the credential the browser produced. `credential` is the attestation response from `navigator.credentials.create()`, passed through unchanged.

credential.description: The WebAuthn attestation response from the browser.

delete_webauthn_credential.title: Delete a passkey
delete_webauthn_credential.description: Remove a passkey from the user's account. If it was their only factor, they may be locked out -- check list_webauthn_credentials and the MFA settings first.

sign_up.title: Register a new user
sign_up.description: Create a user in the pool as a self-service sign-up. Takes the app `client_id` rather than a token, and -- unless the pool auto-confirms -- Cognito emails or texts a confirmation code that confirm_sign_up then needs. If the app client has a secret, `secret_hash` is required.

client_id.description: The user pool app client id the sign-up is for.

username.description: The username, or email address if the pool is configured for email sign-in.

password.description: The user's chosen password. Must satisfy the pool's policy.

user_attributes.description: Attributes to set on the new user, each {"Name": "email", "Value": ...}. Required attributes must be present.

secret_hash.description: The HMAC of username + client id keyed by the client secret. Required when the app client has a secret.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

output.description: Whether the user is already confirmed, their sub, and where the confirmation code was sent.

confirm_sign_up.title: Confirm a new user's registration
confirm_sign_up.description: Complete a sign-up with the code Cognito sent. Until this succeeds the user exists but cannot sign in.

client_id.description: The app client id used for the sign-up.

secret_hash.description: Required when the app client has a secret.

force_alias_creation.description: Move an email or phone alias off another user if it is already taken. Use with care -- it changes how that other user signs in.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

resend_confirmation_code.title: Resend a sign-up confirmation code
resend_confirmation_code.description: Send the sign-up confirmation code again -- a real email or SMS to the user, and rate-limited by the pool.

username.description: The user to resend the code to.

secret_hash.description: Required when the app client has a secret.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

forgot_password.title: Start a password reset
forgot_password.description: Send a user a password-reset code. A real message to a real person, and it only works when the account has a verified email or phone number.

secret_hash.description: Required when the app client has a secret.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

output.description: Where the reset code was sent.

confirm_forgot_password.title: Complete a password reset
confirm_forgot_password.description: Set a new password using the reset code. The user's existing sessions are not invalidated by this alone -- use global_sign_out if the account may have been compromised.

confirmation_code.description: The reset code the user received.

password.description: The new password. Must satisfy the pool's policy.

secret_hash.description: Required when the app client has a secret.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

initiate_auth.title: Start an authentication flow
initiate_auth.description: Begin signing a user in. `auth_flow` picks the mechanism -- "USER_PASSWORD_AUTH" with USERNAME and PASSWORD in `auth_parameters`, "REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH" with REFRESH_TOKEN, "USER_SRP_AUTH" for the SRP exchange. Returns either tokens or a challenge that respond_to_auth_challenge must answer.

auth_parameters.description: Flow parameters, e.g. {"USERNAME": ..., "PASSWORD": ...} or {"REFRESH_TOKEN": ...}, plus SECRET_HASH when the client has a secret.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

session.description: A session from a previous challenge, when continuing a flow.

output.description: Either the issued tokens under `AuthenticationResult`, or the next challenge with its session.

respond_to_auth_challenge.title: Answer an authentication challenge
respond_to_auth_challenge.description: Answer the challenge initiate_auth returned -- an MFA code, a new password, an SRP proof. `challenge_responses` carries the answer and the session ties it to the in-flight attempt.

challenge_name.description: The challenge being answered, as returned by initiate_auth.

client_metadata.description: Extra data passed to the pool's Lambda triggers.

output.description: The issued tokens, or the next challenge.

revoke_token.title: Revoke a refresh token
revoke_token.description: Revoke one refresh token and every access token minted from it. Narrower than global_sign_out, which revokes all of the user's tokens.

client_id.description: The app client id the token was issued to.

client_secret.description: The app client secret, when the client has one.
